CONFIDENTIAL
November 6, 1940.
Assassination of Lieu Tsai Pao and the arrest of
Foo Ping Zung

In connection with the assassination of the
late Lieu Tsai Pao (劉燦波) on September 3, 1940
in the King Hwa Restaurant, 623 Foochow Road,
discreet enquiries show that the crime was per-
petrated by member/s of a guerilla unit which
operated around the suburbs of Shanghai. It has
not been possible to establish whether Foo Ping
Zung (傅炳臣), who was arrested on October 10,
1940 in the French Concession, and who has since
been handed over to the Japanese authorities, was a
member of this guerilla unit, but from information
at our disposal, the local organization of the Blue
Shirt Society has long been non-existent.

Crime Branch Headquarters.

The two suspects, Sung Ts Tsung (孫志忠) and
Tsung Yih Tien (臧一天) have been subjected to frequent
interrogation re the possibility that they may have been
concerned in this offense, they however maintain to their
original statements, which S.M.Police are unable to dis-
prove, their statements re being members of the "Fourth
Route Peace and Construction Army" having been proven
to be correct by a member of the Japanese Gendarmerie.

S.M.Police have no evidence that would warrant
the further detention of these two men, therefore it is
suggested that they be released.

Chinese detectives during the course of daily
routine observation, visiting sources of information
usually available to them despite offer of a reward
to informers that may have led to the arrest of the
persons responsible for this offense fail to obtain
any information that may have led to the arrest of
the persons responsible.

It is recommended that a "Wanted Notice" be
issued by S.M.Police in respect to this offense offer-
ing a substantial reward for any information that may
lead the arrest of the persons responsible for this
offense.

Reference the marginal notes of the
Commissioner of Police. Enquiries show that no
previous notice was given to the restaurant
regarding this tiffin party. The party arrived

deceased was well known at this restaurant, but
not a regular patron, the last time he visited
there being over a month ago.

Regarding Points 1, 2 and 3 mentioned
on Diary 2, Page 3.

There is no record of telephone calls

cannot be ascertained whether or not the deceased
made any telephone call after 11.15 a.m.

The director of the China Film Co., Mr.
Matsuzaki states he cannot point suspicion at any
particular member of the staff. In his opinion
the Wang brothers are above suspicion. They were
very close friends of the deceased and it was in

halls in the company of these two men of an evening.

It has now been definitely ascertained that
the deceased was the manager of the Kou Min Sin Wan
where he was known by the nom-de-plume of Lien Na Er
(刘呐鸥). The Kou Min Sin Wan is situated at 303
Honan Road, not 55 Foochow Road as mentioned in Diary
No. 1 which is the address of the Kou Min News Agency,
an entirely separate concern.

The deceased has occupied the position of
manager of this newspaper since August 4th 1940, having
taken over the position previously occupied by Mu Sae
Ying (穆時英), who was assassinated on Foochow Road
on June 28th 1940 (Subject of Louza F.I.B. 2649/40).
The deceased was a very close friend of the late
Mu Sae Ying.

The assistant manager of the Kou Min Sin Wan
named Go Ling Yu (任麟趾) has been questioned by D.S.
Sugimoto, D.S.I. Fu Chen Yu and the undersigned and
states that the deceased only occasionally visited the
offices of this newspaper. He was last there at about
7 p.m. on 3-9-40 but remained for only about 5 minutes.
No telephone message or other communication was
received from him on the morning of 3-9-40.

Questioned as to his opinion of the murder,
Go Ling Yu stated that he believed it to be a political
assassination instigated by the Chungking Government.

现已确切查明，死者是《国民新闻》的经理，化名为刘呐鸥（刘呐鸥）。《国民新闻》位于河南路303号，而非日记1中提到的福州路55号，后者是《国民通讯社》的地址，两者是完全独立的机构。

自1940年8月4日起，死者一直担任该报社经理，接替了此前由穆时英（穆時英）担任的职位，穆时英于1940年6月28日在福州路被刺杀（参见 Louza F.I.B. 2649/40 案）。死者是已故穆时英的密友。

《国民新闻》副经理任麟趾（任麟趾）接受了副督察长杉本、副督察长傅振宇及本人的问询，他表示死者只是偶尔到访该报社办公室。他最后一次是在1940年9月3日晚上7点左右到达，但仅停留了约5分钟。1940年9月3日上午未收到他的电话留言或其他通讯。

当被问及对谋杀案的看法时，任麟趾表示，他认为这是一起由重庆政府煽动的政治暗杀。

His reason being that Mo Sse Ying, just prior to his
assassination, received a letter threatening him with
death unless the paper cease to publish anti-Chungking
propaganda. As far as can be ascertained the late
Liu Tsai Poo (刘爆皮) did not receive any threats.
However, it cannot be definitely stated that
the motive of this crime was political for the
following reasons :-
Wang Chien (黄谦), one of the persons who
attended the tiffin party at the King Hwa Restaurant,
in a statement made at C.I.D.Q, mentions :-
That at 11.35 a.m. on 3-9-45 (the day of
the murder) the deceased informed him that Mr.
Matsumoto had arrived in Shanghai and suggested that
a tiffin party be held in some restaurant. Wang Chien
requested that this party be held in a restaurant
that was well air conditioned. The deceased then
decided on the King Hwa Restaurant. According to
all the witnesses the deceased did not leave the
office until he went to this tiffin and then proceeded
there in his own motor car. Under these circumstances
he could not have been followed there and thus,
enquiries show that the assassins were waiting in the
restaurant before the arrival of the deceased.
This goes to prove that the information
regarding where the deceased was having tiffin must

他的理由是，穆时英在遇刺前不久收到一封恐吓信，威胁除非该报停止发表反重庆宣传，否则将取其性命。据查，已故刘宰葆（原文拼写错误，应为刘灿波或类似名字，此处照录为刘爆皮）并未收到任何威胁。

午餐聚会在下午2点后不久解散，死者与松崎庆三（Keizo Matsusaki，注：此处名字拼写与前文Keisi Matsumaki略有不同，依原文译作松崎庆三或松崎惠三，前文为Keisi，此处为Keizo，暂统一音译或依字面）最先离开。死者走在后者前面下楼，因为后者在等待聚会的其他成员。当死者走到离底层约第7级台阶时，有人从楼梯底部向他开了三枪。目击者看到两人参与暗杀，但似乎只有一人开枪。随后死者被送往医院，如本报告开头部分所述。本次午餐聚会的成员中，没有人实际目睹枪击或看到

page_data.en:
assassins.
From enquiries made amongst the employees,
the following details of the assassination have
been ascertained.
The two assassins, who are described on page
1, arrived at the restaurant at 12.10 p.m. and
occupied Table 46 which is situated practically
in the middle of the ground floor of the restau-
rant. They later moved to Table 54 which is situ-
ated directly inside the entrance and at the foot
of the stairway. (a plan of the ground floor of
the restaurant is attached). They had food and
drinks including brandy and remained at this table.
At about 2.10 p.m. the door boy named Tsang
(張錦榮)
Pah Yoeng who was sitting on a stool under the
stairway heard some persons coming down the stairs
so got up and walked across to open the door for
them. This witness states that at this point the
two assassins got up from their table, stood at the
foot of the stairs and one of them drew a pistol and
fired three shots. This witness ran towards the
bar and hid, so did not see which way the assassins
escaped. A waiter No.6 Liang Wai Zai, saw a man
who must have been one of the assassins run through
a swing door at the back of the restaurant immediately
page_data.zh:
刺客。
通过对雇员的询问，查明了以下暗杀细节。
第1页描述的两名刺客于中午12时10分到达餐厅，占据了位于餐厅底层几乎中央位置的46号桌。后来他们移到了54号桌，该桌位于入口内侧正对面，楼梯底部。（附有餐厅底层平面图）。他们食用了食物并饮用了包括白兰地在内的饮料，一直待在这张桌子旁。
下午约2时10分，名叫张锦荣（Tsang Pah Yoeng）的门童坐在楼梯下的凳子上，听到有人下楼，便起身走过去为他们开门。这位证人称，此时两名刺客从桌边站起，站在楼梯底部，其中一人拔出手枪开了三枪。这位证人跑向吧台躲藏，因此没有看到刺客从哪个方向逃脱。6号侍者梁伟哉（Liang Wai Zai，音译）看到一名男子（肯定是刺客之一）在枪响后立即穿过餐厅后部的弹簧门，然后穿过宾兴街（Bing Vung Ka，音译，原文如此，可能指北京东路或其他街道的旧称或方言音译）的后门逃跑（见附图）。这位证人当时在茶水间，逃跑的男子差点撞到他。他大声喝令该男子停下，但对方不予理睬。调查未能查明另一名刺客的逃跑路线，但推测他随同那些因枪击而逃离餐厅的顾客从前门离开。

which way the other assassin escaped but it is
presumed that he left by the front door together

Regarding the two suspects arrested by

1. Sung Ts Tsung (孫志忠) 29, Anhwei.

ascertained that they are members of the Peace and

under the authority of 76 Jessfield Road and have

page_data.en:
Keizi Matsusaki
Japan -- D.S.I. Pryde
H. C. C. B. 3-9-40 D.S. Sugimoto

My name is Keizi Matsusaki, age 39, Japanese, and
I am Executive Director and Production Manager of the China
Film Co.

At about 12.30 p.m. on 3-9-40 I had tiffin at the
King Hwa Restaurant, Foochow Road, together with 11 other
members of my company. We finished tiffin at about 2 p.m.
The first to leave the room were Mr. Lieu San Fan (deceased)
and myself. I suggested to Mr. Lieu that we should return
to our office but he stated he had to visit some friends.
Mr. Lieu preceded me down the stairs whilst I waited for
some of the others. Almost immediately afterwards I heard
about three shots and I ran down the stairs and saw Mr. Lieu
lying on the stairs with his shirt front blood stained.
Together with Mr. Horanaki I lifted up Mr. Lieu and placed
him in one of our waiting motor cars. I was going to take
Mr. Lieu to the Pooming Hospital but a Chinese in plainclothes
said a hospital was in the vicinity and this Chinese
accompanied us to the Lester Hospital, Shantung Road. I do
not know the name of this Chinese.

The only words Mr. Lieu spoke to me were "I have
been hit". I left the hospital at about 4 p.m. and came of
my own accord to G.H.Q.

I did not witness the actual shooting and did not
see the assassins.

When the late Mr. Lieu said he intended to visit
his friends, I believe he meant the Kuo Min Sia Wei. It was
the late Mr. Lieu's idea that we should have tiffin at the
King Hwa Restaurant.
page_data.zh:
松崎惠二（Keizi Matsusaki）
日本人 -- 副督察普赖德（Pryde）
中央捕房总部 1940年9月3日 副督察杉本（Sugimoto）

我叫松崎惠二，39岁，日本人，
是中国电影公司执行董事兼制作经理。

1940年9月3日中午12时30分左右，我与本公司其他11名成员在福州路金华酒楼吃午餐。我们在下午2时左右用完午餐。最先离开房间的是刘三藩先生（死者）和我本人。我建议刘先生回办公室，但他说要去拜访朋友。刘先生先我一步下楼，而我则等待其他人。几乎紧接着，我听到大约三声枪响，便跑下楼梯，看见刘先生躺在楼梯上，衬衫前襟染有血迹。我和堀名木先生一起抬起刘先生，将他放入我们的一辆等候的汽车中。我原打算送刘先生去宝隆医院，但一名便衣中国人说附近有一家医院，这名中国人随我们前往山东路的雷士德医院。我不知道这名中国人的姓名。

刘先生对我说的唯一一句话是“我中枪了”。我于下午4时左右离开医院，自愿来到总指挥部。

我没有目击实际开枪过程，也没有看到刺客。

当已故的刘先生表示打算去拜访朋友时，我相信他指的是“国民协维”（Kuo Min Sia Wei）。在金华酒楼吃午餐是已故刘先生的主意。

page_data.en:
Saburo Nozaka
Japanese subject
C.B.H.Q., C.I.    3.9.40

My name is Saburo Nozaka, age 40, Japanese. I am in
charge of the Film Production Affairs Department of the
China Film Co., Hamilton House.
At about 12.30 p.m. 3.9.40 I together with 11 other
members of my company had tiffin in the King Hua Restaurant,
Foochow Road. At approximately 2.15 p.m. we finished tiffin
and were about to depart. Mr. Lieu San Pao, Formosan, was
the first to depart. About one minute later I heard three
shots fired. Mr. Matsuzaki (a member of our party) ran down
the staircase and I followed him and I saw Mr. Lieu San Pao
lying in the middle of the stairway. His shirtfront was
bloodstained. Mr. Matsuzaki, Mr. Kawaguchi and I then picked
up the victim and placed in one of our cars, which was parked
outside the restaurant and he was taken to the Lester Hospital
by Mr. Matsuzaki.
I did not witness the actual shooting.
Later some police arrived on the scene and I together
with the other members of our party went together with the
Police to Louza Police Station.
The late Mr. Lieu was employed as the assistant
manager of the Production Dept. of our Company.
I have also heard that he recently took over the
ownership of the Kua Min Shin Wan.
page_data.zh:
野坂三郎（Saburo Nozaka）
日本籍
中央捕房总部，刑事情报科    1940年9月3日

我叫野坂三郎，40岁，日本人。我负责
中国电影公司（汉密尔顿大楼）的电影制作事务部。
1940年9月3日中午12时30分左右，我与本公司其他11名成员在福州路金华酒楼吃午餐。大约在下午2时15分，我们用完午餐正准备离开。台湾人刘三宝先生最先离开。约一分钟后，我听到三声枪响。松崎先生（我们同行的一员）跑下楼梯，我紧随其后，看见刘三宝先生躺在楼梯中间。他的衬衫前襟染有血迹。随后，松崎先生、川口先生和我抬起受害者，放入停在酒楼外的一辆汽车中，由松崎先生送往雷士德医院。
我没有目击实际开枪过程。
后来一些警察到达现场，我与同行的其他成员一起随警察前往老闸捕房。
已故的刘先生受雇为我公司制作部副经理。
我还听说他最近接管了“华民新湾”（Kua Min Shin Wan）的所有权。

Wang Chien (黄谦.)
Canton
H. Q. C. B. 3-9-40 translated Z. P. Tseung

My name is Wang Chien, age 34 years, native of
Canton, and residing at House 67, Lane 608, Yu Yuen Road.
I am an employee of the Chung Hwa Motion Picture
Coy.
At about 10 a.m. on the 3-9-40 I accompanied my
elder brother Wang Zai Tae to the general office of the Chang
Hua Motion Picture Coy. situated at Kiangsu Road, where we are
working at present.
At approximately 11 a.m. Mr. Lieu Tsui Pee also
attended the office and later he was busily engaged in
communicating with others over the telephone. At about 11.15
a.m. he told me that Mr. Matsumoto, the director, had arrived
in Shanghai and suggested that we could have tiffin at some
restaurant where the making of a film would be the topic of
our discussion. I suggested that he should select a
restaurant where there was no cooling system, as I had just
recovered from my sickness. In view of this, Mr. Lieu decided
to give the dinner at the King Hwa Restaurant, Foochow Road.
At about 12.30 p.m. accompanied by six others including
Messrs. Matsusaki, Matsumoto etc., I proceeded to this
restaurant. Mr. Lieu, who had not completed his work, promised
to attend the party a little while later. After a few minutes
Mr. Lieu came to the restaurant as promised. After having
finished our tiffin, Mr. Lieu, carrying a leather case in
his hand, left the room and proceeded downstairs. He was then
followed by Mr. Matsusaki. At this juncture I heard the sound
of three gun shots, and immediately ran to the verandah, where

王谦（Wang Chien）(黄谦.)
广东籍
总部 中央捕房 1940年9月3日 翻译 谢Z.P.

我叫王谦，34岁，广东籍，居住于愚园路608弄67号。
我是中华电影公司的雇员。
1940年9月3日上午10时左右，我陪同我的哥哥王才泰前往位于江苏路的中华电影公司总办事处，我们目前在那里工作。
大约上午11时，刘翠皮先生也来到办公室，随后他忙于与他人通电话。大约上午11时15分，他告诉我导演松本先生已抵达上海，并建议我们可以去一家餐馆吃午餐，以便讨论电影制作事宜。我建议他选择一家没有冷气设备的餐馆，因为我刚病愈。鉴于此，刘先生决定在福州路金华酒楼设宴。

page_data.en:
Wang Zai Tso (黄才初)
Canton
H . . J. B.    3-9-40    translated    C. P. Tsalling

My name is Wang Zai Tso, age 35 years, native
of Canton and residing at No. 33 Jessfield Road.
I am the sub-manager of the Business Department
of the Chung Hwa Motion Picture Coy.
At 12 noon on the 3-9-40, I accompanied eleven
others, including Lieu Tsai Poo, K. Matsusaki etc., who
are on the staff of this motion picture Co., to have tiffin
at the King Hwa Restaurant, Foochow Road, where we discussed
problems relating to the manuscript of a play. Our party
was concluded at 2.10 p.m. as Mr. Matsusaki had to leave
to attend another appointment. Lieu Tsai Poo, Matsusaki and
Kawaguchi were the first to leave the room, whilst the rest
of us followed suit. In doing so I heard the sound of three
gun shots just below the staircase, whereupon I immediately
ran to the verandah and looking downwards I saw a Police van
stopped at the entrance of the restaurant. Shortly afterwards
Mr. Kawaguchi came upstairs and informed us that Lieu Tsai
Poo had been the victim of a shooting and sent to a
hospital for treatment.
I did not witness the actual shooting. Late Mr.
Lieu was the Assistant Manager of the Production Dept. of
our company.
sgd. : Wang Zai Tso

广东籍
总部 . . J. B.    1940年9月3日    翻译    C. P. Tsalling

我叫王才初，35岁，广东籍，居住于极司菲尔路33号。
我是中华电影公司业务部副经理。
1940年9月3日中午12时，我陪同包括刘载甫、K. 松崎等在内的本公司其他十一名职员，前往福州路金华酒楼吃午餐，期间我们讨论了与剧本有关的问题。由于松崎先生需离开赴另一约会，我们的聚会在下午2时10分结束。刘载甫、松崎和川口最先离开房间，其余人随后跟进。在此过程中，我听到楼梯下方传来三声枪响，随即立即跑到阳台，向下望去，看见一辆警车停在酒楼门口。不久后，川口先生上楼通知我们，刘载甫遭枪击并被送往医院治疗。

Sung Yah Ling (沈雅琳)
Chekiang
C.S.H. G., C.1.    3.9.40    translated    Hsu B. F.

My name is Sung Yah Ling, aged 23 years, native of
Chekiang, and employed as a typist at the Chun Hwa Motion
Picture Company, Hamilton House.

At 12 noon on the 3.9.40 I together with some other
employees of the above company proceeded to the "Ching Hua"
Restaurant, Foochow Road, where we had our tiffin.

We finished tiffin at 2.10 p.m. same date and then
started to leave the restaurant with Lieu Tsai Poo (deceased)
walking in front of all. No sooner had I descended one step of
the staircase in the restaurant than I heard three sounds of
gun shots and simultaneously saw heard Lieu Tsai Poo (now
deceased) shouting out "Pain, pain". On seeing this Messrs
Matsuzaki and Sasaki rushed to the deceased and carried him
to a r/car.

I did not witness the actual shooting.

Late Mr. Lieu was the Assistant Manager of the
Production Dept. of the company.

I have been employed as a door boy for over one year
by the Ching Hua (清華) Cantonese Restaurant, 823 Foochow Road.
My duty is to open the door for incoming and out-going
patrons. For this purpose I am allowed to sit on a stool near
the foot of the staircase and in full view of the main and
only door.
At about 2.10 p.m. September 3, 1940 I was sitting
on my stool when I heard some one descending the stairs. I
turned, to see who it was because boys also use the stairs.
Seeing an old male customer named Liam descending, followed
by three male Japanese and one female Chinese, I got off my
stool and made to go to the front door to assist them in what-
ever they might want such as opening car doors etc. As I did
so I saw two male Chinese stand up from a table just to the
right of the door (on going in) and one of them nearest the
door, but with his back to it, turned and stepped forward a
pace or so and took out a revolver which he had kept on his
left side and fired three shots in the direction of Mr. Liam
who was landing and, at the time of the shooting, was about
half way down the stairs.
I immediately ran behind the counter of the bar, which
is behind my stool, and crouched there.
Hearing no further shots, I made my way to the foot
of the stairs and saw Mr. Liam lying on the stairs bleeding
profusely from the chest. Two of the Japanese who had followed
Mr. Liam down, lifted him and carried him to a private motor
car (number unknown). As they were doing this, Police arrived.

我在福州路823号清华粤菜馆受雇担任门童已有一年多。
我的职责是为进出顾客开门。为此，我获准坐在楼梯脚附近的一张凳子上，正对着主要且唯一的出入口。
1940年9月3日下午2时10分左右，我正坐在凳子上，这时听到有人下楼。我转身想看是谁，因为伙计们也使用楼梯。我看见一位名叫林（Liam）的年长男顾客走下来，身后跟着三名日本男子和一名中国女子，我便从凳子上起身，准备走向前门协助他们做任何可能需要的事，如开车门等。就在我这样做时，我看见两名中国男子从门口右侧（进门方向）的一张桌子旁站起来，其中离门最近但背对门的那人转过身，向前迈了一步左右，从左侧掏出一把左轮手枪，朝正在下楼的林先生开了三枪，开枪时林先生大约在楼梯半中间。
我立即跑到吧台柜台后面躲起来，吧台位于我的凳子后方。
听到没有进一步的枪声后，我走到楼梯底部，看见林先生躺在楼梯上，胸部大量出血。跟随林先生下楼的兩名日本人中的两人抬起他，将他送入一辆私家车（车牌号不详）。当他们这样做时，警察到达了。

I have been employed as a waitress at the Ching Hua
Restaurant, 623 Foochow Road for over one year.
I attend to tables 52, 54 and 55. Table 54 is immediate-
ly on the right of the main door on going into the restaurant.
Table 52 is the one next to it and table 55 is one used only
at busy times.
At about 12.10 p.m. Sept. 3, 1940, two male Chinese
entered the restaurant and proceeded to table 46.
After sitting at the table for about five minutes, the
two males saw table 54 was then unoccupied and they called me
to move their glasses of tea to table 54 and explained they
had already ordered food to the value of $5.00.
A few minutes later the male sitting nearest the door,
and with his back to it, ordered a brandy ($3.80), a bottle of
lemonade and two glasses. The two shared the brandy which they
mixed with the lemonade.
They finished eating at about 1.45 p.m. and paid the
bill of $8.85 and told me to keep the change from $11.00 as
I cleared the table. The male nearest the door asked for a
packet of Capstan cigarettes and told me to keep the change
from $2.00.
I then took up my usual position near the bar counter,
and a few minutes later (about 2.10 p.m.) filled up the two males'
glasses of tea with hot water. I took the bottles into the
pantry at the rear and whilst there heard several shots fired
in the restaurant.
On the shooting ceasing, I went out and saw that the

我在福州路623号清华酒楼受雇担任女侍应已有一年多。
我负责52、54和55号桌。54号桌紧邻进门后的主门右侧。52号桌是紧挨着的一张，55号桌仅在繁忙时使用。
1940年9月3日中午12时10分左右，两名中国男子进入酒楼，走向46号桌。
在桌旁坐了约五分钟后，这两名男子见54号桌当时空着，便叫我将其茶杯移至54号桌，并解释他们已点了价值5.00元的食物。
几分钟后，坐得离门最近且背对门的那名男子点了一杯白兰地（3.80元）、一瓶柠檬水和两个杯子。两人分享了混有柠檬水的白兰地。
他们在下午1时45分左右吃完，支付了8.85元的账单，并在我清理桌子时告诉我不用找还11.00元的零钱。离门最近的男子要了一包卡普斯坦（Capstan）香烟，并告诉我不用找还2.00元的零钱。
随后我回到吧台柜台附近的常规位置，几分钟后（约下午2时10分）为这两名男子的茶杯添满热水。我将瓶子拿到后面的餐具室，在那里时听到酒楼内响起几声枪响。
枪声停止后，我走出去，看见

I have been employed as assistant head waiter
No. 6 on the ground floor of the King Hua Restaurant, 623
Foochow Road, for over one year.

At about 2.10 p.m. September 3, 1940 I was in the
pantry off from the restaurant sorting napkins etc. when I
heard the sound of shots fired in the restaurant.
I immediately hurried to the swing door separating the
pantry from the restaurant and was about to push the door
before me when it was violently pushed towards me by someone
on the other side.

I automatically stepped back a pace and I then
saw a male Chinese wearing a grey foreign-style suit run
towards the kitchen which is beside the pantry and adjoins
a small alley which gives access to Sing Vong Rd. I, thinking
the male was a terrified patron, called to him to stop
running but this was ignored and the man passed out of my
sight.

I proceeded into the restaurant with the intention
of closing the front door and on the stairs saw two Japanese
males carrying a male Chinese whom they placed in a private
motor car, number unknown.

A few moments later, Police arrived.

I do not know whether the male I saw running into
the kitchen was the man who did the shooting or not.

I cannot recall his description.

我在福州路623号金华餐厅 (King Hua Restaurant) 一楼
担任副领班（第6号侍者）已有一年多。

1940年9月3日下午2点10分左右，我正在餐厅旁的
餐具间整理餐巾等物品，这时我听到餐厅内传来枪声。
我立即冲向分隔餐具间与餐厅的弹簧门，正欲推开门时，
门被另一侧的人猛烈地向我推来。

我不由自主地向后退了一步，随后看见一名身穿灰色西式西装的
华籍男子跑向厨房，厨房紧邻餐具间，并通向一条可通往
新旺路 (Sing Vong Rd.) 的小巷。我以为该男子是受惊的顾客，
便喊他停下奔跑，但他置之不理，随即消失在我的视线中。

我走进餐厅，打算关闭前门，在楼梯上看见两名日本男子
抬着一名华籍男子，并将他放入一辆私人汽车中，车牌号不详。

片刻之后，警察赶到。

我不知道我看见跑进厨房的那名男子是否就是开枪者。

我想不起他的体貌特征。

I have been employed as waiter No. 12 at the King

Shortly after 12 noon September 3, 1940 I was on
duty on the first floor when an old patron, Mr. Lieu and
two brothers named Wong, also old customers, came upstairs

to me and I called waiter 36 and learned he wanted the bill.

Gerald Owen Wootten, British, was born in
London on October 2, 1894. He is an architect
by profession and came to Shanghai some time
after the Great War. He set up in business
as an architect with a Spanish citizen named
La Fuente and on the death of the latter went
into partnership with a British subject named
Patstone who also died. In 1928 he was
the manager of the Compagnie Oriental de
Capitalisation, a savings society which closed
down that year following the discovery of fraudulent
conversion and litigation by the bond and share
holders in the U.S. Consular Court. Wootten,
however, is believed to have had no criminal
responsibility in this matter.

Ollerdenen, member of a well-known American
Eurasian family in Shanghai. They had a
daughter of the same name who is still in Shanghai

who for some time had been on bad terms with his
wife, left her and proceeded to the States with a
Russian girl who was his paramour. In America
he obtained a divorce from Mrs. M. Wootten, the
legal validity of which is doubtful, and married
his Russian paramour. It is understood that
he has since been divorced from the latter. He
